relation.title: Relation
relation.summary: Declares a named predicate: rules derive which of its tuples hold.
relation.note: `key(c)` is an integrity constraint: two accepted tuples with the same key and different other arguments give `KEY_CONFLICT`; nothing is chosen or dropped. `kind` is analysis metadata and does not change truth.

rule.title: Inference rule
rule.summary: Derives a conclusion when its conditions hold.
rule.note: `strict` conclusions cannot be defeated by priority. Use `defeasible` for rules that admit exceptions.

when.title: Body clause
when.summary: Conjoins the conditions a rule needs: literals, comparisons, calls.
when.note: Every variable the head concludes must be bound by a positive body conjunct; an unbound head variable is a static error.

then.title: Rule head
then.summary: States what the rule concludes: a literal or a norm template.
then.note: A `defeater` rule has no `then`: it carries `defeat` instead.

strict.title: Strict strength
strict.summary: An indefeasible consequence inside the chosen theory.
strict.note: Two strict rules with opposite conclusions keep a strict conflict; priority does not resolve it.

defeasible.title: Defeasible strength
defeasible.summary: A candidate consequence that a stronger opposite can defeat.
defeasible.note: Most legal general rules and presumptions should be defeasible.

defeater.title: Defeater rule
defeater.summary: Blocks a conclusion without supporting its complement.
defeater.note: A defeater carries `defeat`, never `then`; production rules must declare strength explicitly.

key.neutral.title: Key declaration
key.neutral.summary: Names the arguments that identify a tuple or a generated node.
key.neutral.note: One spelling, two meanings: in a relation it constrains identity, in an expansion path it names the case. Check the role before editing.

key.relation.title: Relation key
key.relation.summary: Declares the candidate key: one key projection identifies one tuple.
key.relation.note: Two different non-key projections over one accepted key tuple are a KEY_CONFLICT; the evaluator never silently picks a value.

key.expansion.title: Expansion case key
key.expansion.summary: Names the generated node after the case: `key(c)` is the case name.
key.expansion.note: The id carries no ordinal, coordinates, or package digest; adding a case never renames existing nodes.

package.title: Package declaration
package.summary: Names the package and pins the language version; every file belongs to exactly one package.
package.note: The name is ASCII lowercase dotted segments; hard §15 keywords are allowed inside. Published registry packages use two or more segments; one segment is for local packages.

import.title: Dependency import
import.summary: Declares a dependency once per package; only its pub symbols become reachable as pkg::Symbol.
import.note: Repeat imports are LDC-E1103, self-import LDC-E1102. check does not judge dependencies (E-0126); lower needs the resolve context. The law.std prelude needs no import.

namespace.title: Namespace declaration
namespace.summary: URI from which declaration StableIds are built ({namespace}#{Name}); one package forms one tree.
namespace.note: The public namespace comes from the manifest URI: renaming a package must not change existing public @ids.

entity.title: Nominal entity type
entity.summary: Declares a nominal type: identity is the pair (type, stable id); equal ids in two types never mix.
entity.note: Declare only intrinsic immutable payload; temporal or disputable traits belong in relations. Address pinned individuals with entity_ref.

event.title: Event declaration
event.summary: Desugars to an immutable nominal entity with id and typed fields; executable use wants one canonical time interval.
event.note: Instances are immutable; a correction creates a new version with provenance (§81.1). Prefer entity_ref when a pinned snapshot supplies the payload.

function.title: Pure function
function.summary: Returns a data value, never a proposition; pure means no assertions, no norms, no ambient reads.
function.note: pure demands proved purity, bare function asks for inference; both lower only with a proved PURE_DETERMINISTIC call graph. Model sourced attributes as relations instead.

type.title: Type alias
type.summary: Names an existing type without nominal separation; transparency holds on both compiler stages.
type.note: For a legally significant distinction use entity or a newtype profile. Alias cycles break on name repeat; foreign-package aliases resolve like any qualified reference.

expansion.title: Expansion definition
expansion.summary: A closed generation profile: params plus emit rules that generate nodes with stable ids, labels and anchors.
expansion.note: 0.1 admits no open macros and no text pasting; 0.2 (§279.2) is additive. Case keys name the generated nodes.

facts.title: Exported fact group
facts.summary: Named unit for exporting facts across the package border; the body holds asserts only.
facts.note: Inclusion is an explicit facts pkg::Group line — never a silent merge. Group nodes materialize byte-identically with producer provenance; membership is counted by the resolver.

query.title: Query declaration
query.summary: A named query declaration is reserved in the executable slice; use an explicit §172 query input.
query.note: Source refuses the declaration with E1321; active evaluation refuses QUERY_DECL_NON_EXECUTABLE. The full-model §173 shape is not an executable function.

Number.title: Exact number
Number.summary: The single exact numeric domain of 0.4 programs: every numeric spelling is one value, carried as an irreducible fraction.
Number.note: `1`, `1.0` and `2/2` are one value and one key. Programs 0.2/0.3 keep their own rules; mixing 0.4 values with earlier families without an explicit adapter is rejected.

Algebraic.title: Exact algebraic real
Algebraic.summary: An exact algebraic real number: a minimal polynomial plus the index of its real root.
Algebraic.note: Always irrational: a rational result reduces to `Number`. Built by `exact_sqrt`; a literal is read only with an irreducible polynomial.

RealExpr.title: Symbolic real expression
RealExpr.summary: A symbolic real expression over exact leaves and named constants such as `pi()` and `ln2()`.
RealExpr.note: Comparison is proven or refused (`UNPROVEN`), never guessed. Rounding publishes only a whole cell. A `RealExpr` value is not a key.

Currency.title: Currency
Currency.summary: The currency of a `Money` amount — the code in a literal such as `1000000 KZT`.
Currency.note: Not written as a type: `c: Currency` does not resolve (`LDC-E2101`). Arithmetic between different currencies is `CURRENCY_MISMATCH`.

exact_sqrt.title: Exact square root
exact_sqrt.summary: Exact square root of a rational argument; takes no precision profile.

params.name: value
params.doc: A rational number; a negative one is `DOMAIN_ERROR`.

exact_sqrt.note: A perfect square folds to `Number`; a negative argument is `DOMAIN_ERROR`; otherwise the result is `Algebraic`. Available from profile 0.4.

pi.title: Constant π
pi.summary: The constant π as an exact symbolic value, without rounding.
pi.note: Returns a `RealExpr` leaf (profile 0.5). Numeric bounds come from certificate composition over the profiles `p8 → p16 → p32`.

ln2.title: Constant ln 2
ln2.summary: The constant ln 2 as an exact symbolic value, without rounding.
ln2.note: Returns a `RealExpr` leaf (profile 0.5). Numeric bounds come from certificate composition over the profiles `p8 → p16 → p32`.

solve_linear.title: Linear equation root
solve_linear.summary: The root of `a·x + b = 0` over the rationals.
solve_linear.note: Coefficients are Integer, Number, Rational or Decimal; the root is an exact `Number`. A degenerate equation is `DOMAIN_ERROR`. Available from profile 0.6.

temp_convert.title: Exact temperature conversion
temp_convert.summary: Exact temperature conversion under an explicit versioned policy.

params.name: role
params.doc: `absolute` for a point, `difference` for a delta.

params.name: policy
params.doc: The versioned policy tag, for example `units/0.7`.

temp_convert.note: `role` is declared, never inferred: `absolute` is a point (affine, from 0 K; below zero is `DOMAIN_ERROR`), `difference` is a delta (pure scale). An unknown `policy` tag is a `TYPE_ERROR`.

angle_convert.title: Exact angle conversion
angle_convert.summary: Exact angle conversion under an explicit versioned policy.

params.name: policy
params.doc: The versioned policy tag, for example `units/0.7`.

angle_convert.note: The result is always a symbolic `RealExpr` through `pi`, with no reduction. `policy` is a tag from a closed set (`units/0.7`); an unknown tag is a `TYPE_ERROR`.

magnitude.title: Quantity to Magnitude
magnitude.summary: Lifts a `Quantity` into the dimension algebra as a `Magnitude`.

params.name: q
params.doc: A `Quantity` whose unit tag resolves in the unit registry.

magnitude.note: The unit tag must resolve in the §49.2 unit registry; an opaque legal tag such as `mrp` or `business_day` gives `UNIT_UNKNOWN`.

count.title: Count aggregate
count.summary: Counts the elements of a collection; an empty collection gives 0.
count.note: Short form: `count distinct o: Order for a: Money where F`. Unlike `sum`, `min` and `max`, an empty `count` is not an `EMPTY_AGGREGATE`.

max.title: Maximum aggregate
max.summary: The largest value of a collection.

params.name: xs
params.doc: The collection to take the largest value of.

max.note: An empty collection gives `EMPTY_AGGREGATE` unless the full form names the policy: `max(xs, empty: 0 KZT)`. The collection stays the first positional argument.

min.title: Minimum aggregate
min.summary: The smallest value of a collection.

params.name: xs
params.doc: The collection to take the smallest value of.

min.note: An empty collection gives `EMPTY_AGGREGATE` unless the full form names the policy: `min(xs, empty: 0 KZT)`. The collection stays the first positional argument.

sum.title: Sum aggregate
sum.summary: Exact sum of a collection of `Decimal`, `Money` or `Quantity` values.
sum.note: An empty collection gives `EMPTY_AGGREGATE` unless the policy is named: `sum(xs, empty: 0 KZT)`. Short form: `sum all a: Money for o: Order where F`.

round.title: Rounding under a policy
round.summary: Rounds an already computed value to a precision under a named mode.

params.name: value
params.doc: The already computed value to round.

round.note: Rounding is never implied: an inexact monetary result must name its policy. To divide under a policy use `div_round` — `/` may fail before `round` has anything to round.

div_round.title: Division under a policy
div_round.summary: Divides and rounds the exact quotient to a precision under a named mode.

params.name: dividend
params.doc: The amount or number to divide.

params.name: divisor
params.doc: The divisor; with `Money / Money` both amounts share one currency.

div_round.note: Rounding is applied always, not only when the quotient is inexact. `Money / Money` of one currency gives a dimensionless share; `Integer / Integer` and `Rational / Rational` are not accepted.

add_calendar_period.title: Calendar step
add_calendar_period.summary: Steps a date by a calendar period: days, weeks, months or years.
add_calendar_period.note: Calendar units only; business_day is TYPE_ERROR. The calendar snapshot is not read. Negative literal counts are LDC-E3102; negative variable counts refuse with DEADLINE_POLICY_INVALID.

add_business_days.title: Business-day step
add_business_days.summary: Steps a date by counted days under the calendar snapshot and the deadline policy.
add_business_days.note: Requires a calendar snapshot; missing policy is MISSING_POLICY. Only business_day/calendar_day are accepted; other units are TYPE_ERROR. Negative literals are LDC-E3102; negative variable counts refuse with DEADLINE_POLICY_INVALID.

days_between.title: Days between dates
days_between.summary: Number of calendar days from `from` to `to`; negative when `to` precedes `from`.
days_between.note: A core term: a penalty per day of delay is computed inside the rule instead of being asserted as a case fact.

year_start_of.title: Start of the year
year_start_of.summary: January 1 of the calendar year containing the date.
year_start_of.note: The calendar snapshot and the deadline policy are not consulted. Executable under semantics 0.2 only.

year_end_of.title: End of the year
year_end_of.summary: December 31 of the calendar year containing the date.
year_end_of.note: The calendar snapshot and the deadline policy are not consulted. Executable under semantics 0.2 only.

month_start_of.title: Start of the month
month_start_of.summary: The first day of the month containing the date.
month_start_of.note: The calendar snapshot and the deadline policy are not consulted.

month_end_of.title: End of the month
month_end_of.summary: The last day of the month containing the date.
month_end_of.note: The calendar snapshot and the deadline policy are not consulted.

weekday_of.title: Day of week
weekday_of.summary: Day of week of a date as an integer from 1 (Monday) to 7 (Sunday).
weekday_of.note: ISO 8601 numbering. The argument is `Date` only; the result is an `Integer`.

add_legal_term.title: Legal term step
add_legal_term.summary: Steps a date by a legal term, choosing the operation by the unit of the term.

params.name: term
params.doc: A `Quantity` whose unit selects the operation.

add_legal_term.note: `business_day` and `calendar_day` run under `add_business_days` rules; `calendar_week`, `calendar_month` and `calendar_year` under `add_calendar_period` rules. Semantics 0.2 only.

add_duration.title: Instant plus duration
add_duration.summary: The instant that lies a physical duration after `after`.
add_duration.note: The only step from an `Instant`: it adds physical time, not a calendar period or a business day, and reads neither the calendar nor the deadline policy. Semantics 0.2 only.

hours_between.title: Hours between instants
hours_between.summary: Number of full hours between two instants; negative when the order is reversed.
hours_between.note: Counts FULL hours, truncating toward zero; both arguments are `Instant`. For minute precision use `minutes_between`.

minutes_between.title: Minutes between instants
minutes_between.summary: Number of full minutes between two instants, with the sign and truncation of `hours_between`.
minutes_between.note: Both arguments are `Instant`; the count truncates toward zero.

convert.title: Unit conversion
convert.summary: Converts a `Quantity` to another unit by the exact factor `num/den`.

params.name: num
params.doc: Numerator of the exact factor: a strictly positive `Integer`.

params.name: den
params.doc: Denominator of the exact factor: a strictly positive `Integer`.

params.name: unit
params.doc: The non-empty `Text` tag of the target unit.

convert.note: `value` is `Quantity` only — `Money` is rejected by name. `num` and `den` are strictly positive `Integer`s; `unit` is the non-empty target tag. No factor registry checks the pair.

with_unit.title: Attach a unit
with_unit.summary: Turns a dimensionless number into a `Quantity` of the named unit.

params.name: unit
params.doc: The non-empty `Text` tag of the unit.

with_unit.note: `value` is `Integer`, `Decimal` or a 10-smooth `Rational`. A value that already has a unit is rejected by name — retagging is only `convert`.

unit_convert.title: Convert within a dimension
unit_convert.summary: Converts a `Magnitude` to another unit of the same dimension.

params.name: unit
params.doc: The target unit, resolved in the unit registry.

unit_convert.note: Source and target dimensions must match, otherwise `UNIT_DIMENSION_MISMATCH`. The scale ratio is exact, so no dated factor registry is involved.

scalar_of.title: Magnitude to number
scalar_of.summary: A magnitude of zero dimension as an exact `Rational`.
scalar_of.note: A nonzero dimension gives `UNIT_DIMENSION_MISMATCH`. This is the only way out of the algebra into plain numbers.

quantity_of.title: Magnitude to Quantity
quantity_of.summary: Turns a `Magnitude` back into a `Quantity` of the named unit.

params.name: unit
params.doc: The unit whose expansion must match the magnitude.

quantity_of.note: Checked, not relabeled: the factors of the magnitude must match the expansion of the unit, otherwise `UNIT_MISMATCH`.

unit_exponent.title: Exponent of a unit
unit_exponent.summary: The exponent of a simple unit in the factors of a magnitude, as an exact `Integer`.

params.name: unit
params.doc: A simple unit, or an alias of one.

unit_exponent.note: A derived unit is rejected with `UNIT_MISMATCH` (it has no single exponent); an unknown name gives `UNIT_UNKNOWN`.

text_length.title: Text length
text_length.summary: Number of code points of a text after NFC normalization.
text_length.note: The unit is the code point, not the byte or the grapheme cluster; an empty string gives 0.

round_bounds.title: Round an interval
round_bounds.summary: Rounds certified bounds to a single value at a precision.
round_bounds.note: Succeeds only when both ends round to the same value; otherwise `BOUNDS_INSUFFICIENT` names both extreme values.

ln_bounds.title: Logarithm bounds
ln_bounds.summary: Certified bounds of the natural logarithm of `x`.
ln_bounds.note: `x` must be a dimensionless number greater than 0 (`DOMAIN_ERROR` otherwise); `Quantity`, `Money` and `Magnitude` are rejected by name. A profile outside the closed set is `UNIT_PROFILE_UNKNOWN`.

exp_bounds.title: Exponential bounds
exp_bounds.summary: Certified bounds of `e` to the power `x`, for any sign of `x`.
exp_bounds.note: `profile` names the precision from a closed versioned set such as `p8/0.1`; a profile outside the set is `UNIT_PROFILE_UNKNOWN`.

sqrt_bounds.title: Square root bounds
sqrt_bounds.summary: Certified bounds of the square root of `x`.
sqrt_bounds.note: `x < 0` gives `DOMAIN_ERROR`. An exact root returns a degenerate interval.

pi_bounds.title: Bounds of π
pi_bounds.summary: Certified bounds of π at the precision of a profile.
pi_bounds.note: `profile` names the precision from a closed versioned set such as `p8/0.1`; a profile outside the set is `UNIT_PROFILE_UNKNOWN`.

sin_bounds.title: Sine bounds
sin_bounds.summary: Certified bounds of the sine of `x`.
sin_bounds.note: Computed together with `cos_bounds` by one algorithm. A profile outside the closed versioned set is `UNIT_PROFILE_UNKNOWN`.

cos_bounds.title: Cosine bounds
cos_bounds.summary: Certified bounds of the cosine of `x`.
cos_bounds.note: Computed together with `sin_bounds` by one algorithm. A profile outside the closed versioned set is `UNIT_PROFILE_UNKNOWN`.

bounds_add.title: Add bounds
bounds_add.note: Composes two `Bounds`; the derivation of the result records both operands, so the certificate stays checkable.

bounds_sub.title: Subtract bounds
bounds_sub.note: The ends cross over: the lower end subtracts the upper end of the other interval.

bounds_mul.title: Multiply bounds
bounds_mul.note: The result is `[min p, max p]` over the four end products `a.lo·b.lo`, `a.lo·b.hi`, `a.hi·b.lo`, `a.hi·b.hi`.

bounds_div.title: Divide bounds

params.name: b
params.doc: The divisor `Bounds`; it must not contain zero.

bounds_div.note: A divisor interval that contains zero is rejected with `DIVISION_BY_ZERO`. A base-10 logarithm is a composition: `div(ln(x), ln(10))`.

bounds_scale.title: Scale bounds
bounds_scale.summary: Multiplies an interval by the exact factor `num/den`.

params.name: den
params.doc: Denominator of the exact factor; zero is `DIVISION_BY_ZERO`.

bounds_scale.note: A negative factor swaps the ends; `den = 0` is `DIVISION_BY_ZERO`. `num` and `den` are exact dimensionless numbers.

bounds_const.title: Exact value as bounds
bounds_const.summary: The degenerate interval `[f, f]` for the exact number `f = num/den`.
bounds_const.note: Brings a literal of the norm into a bounds formula. `num` and `den` are exact dimensionless `Integer`, `Decimal` or `Rational`.

Text.title: Text value
Text.summary: A text value; text is NFC-normalized.
Text.note: Length is counted by `text_length` in code points, not bytes. A unit tag or a policy name passed to a std term is a non-empty `Text`.

Integer.title: Integer
Integer.note: Unlike `Rational`, an `Integer` has a value limit named by §58. Exact division yields `Rational`, never a silently rounded `Integer`.

Decimal.title: Decimal number
Decimal.summary: An exact decimal number, written as a literal such as `0.20`.
Decimal.note: `Decimal / Decimal` stays `Decimal` only for a 10-smooth denominator; otherwise the result is an exact `Rational`. Rounding is never implied — use `round` or `div_round`.

Rational.title: Exact rational
Rational.summary: An exact rational value: the result type of exact division, serialized as an irreducible fraction.
Rational.note: Not bounded in bit width; unbounded use is stopped by the §238 resource counters with `RESOURCE_LIMIT` and no partial result.

Money.title: Money amount
Money.summary: An amount in a named currency, written as a literal such as `1000000 KZT`.
Money.note: Arithmetic between different currencies is `CURRENCY_MISMATCH`; conversion needs a rate, a date and a snapshot. Rounding is never implied.

Quantity.title: Quantity with a unit
Quantity.summary: A number with a unit tag, written as a literal such as `300 km`.
Quantity.note: Comparing or adding different units is a `TYPE_ERROR`; conversion is only explicit (`convert`). The type takes no parameter: `Quantity<Mass>` is `LDC-E2118`.

Date.title: Calendar date
Date.note: Placing a `Date` on the time axis needs a §82.1 resolution policy; without it evaluation stops with `TEMPORAL_RESOLUTION_POLICY_MISSING`, never a silent fallback to UTC.

Instant.title: Instant
Instant.summary: A point on the time axis, written with an offset: `@2026-03-31T18:00:00+05:00`.
Instant.note: The written offset is representation, not identity: the same moment in another offset is the same value, and order follows the moment, not the wall clock.

Duration.title: Physical duration
Duration.summary: A physical duration in seconds and nanoseconds.
Duration.note: Not a calendar period: months and years are `CalendarPeriod`, working days are `BusinessPeriod`. `add_duration` is the only step from an `Instant`.

Boolean.title: Boolean
Boolean.note: The result of a relation is not `Boolean`: it is a proposition evaluated as `TRUE_ONLY`, `FALSE_ONLY`, `BOTH` or `NEITHER`.

Timezone.title: Time zone
Timezone.summary: An IANA time zone name such as `Asia/Qyzylorda`.
Timezone.note: Only the portable name subset is accepted; whether the zone exists in tzdb is not checked by the profile.

LanguageTag.title: Language tag
LanguageTag.summary: A BCP-47 language tag such as `kk-KZ`.
LanguageTag.note: Casing is canonicalized for comparison while the original spelling is kept. Grandfathered and private-use tags need a feature profile.

Jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction
Jurisdiction.summary: The type of a jurisdictional binding: a code that names a legal order.
Jurisdiction.note: A library type of `law.std.data`, not an actor and not a core built-in type. The constant is written with a record literal: `Jurisdiction { code: "KZ" }`.

List.title: List
List.summary: An ordered collection that allows duplicates.
List.note: Iteration that affects a result must have a deterministic order. The element type is written as a parameter: `List<Date>`.

Set.title: Set
Set.note: Iteration that affects a result must have a deterministic order. The element type is written as a parameter: `Set<Text>`.

Option.title: Optional value
Option.summary: An optional value: there is no `null`, absence is `Option<T>`.
Option.note: One of the seven std names that take a parameter; a parameter on any other std name is `LDC-E2118`.

Magnitude.title: Dimensioned magnitude
Magnitude.summary: A value whose dimension is computed from the unit registry, with product, quotient and conversion.
Magnitude.note: Enter the algebra with `magnitude(q)` and leave it with `quantity_of` or `scalar_of`; `Quantity * Quantity` itself stays an error (`LDC-E2108`).

Bounds.title: Certified bounds
Bounds.summary: A closed rational interval bundled with the derivation that produced it.
Bounds.note: A record literal in `Bounds` position is a `TYPE_ERROR`; on read the bounds are recomputed from the derivation, and a mismatch is `BOUNDS_CERTIFICATE_INVALID`.

text.fragment.title: Fragment text
text.fragment.summary: The pinned official text of a fragment, in a named language and status.
text.fragment.note: `content_hash` is the sha256 of the exact text bytes; when the edition declares pinned bytes, a fragment without it is rejected (`LDC-E5205`).

text.amendment.title: Amendment text
text.amendment.summary: The new text an amendment operation puts at a locator.
text.amendment.note: Applying the operations to the previous edition must yield the next one; a divergence is `LDC-E5401`, and neither text is accepted automatically.

uri.title: Publication address
uri.summary: The canonical address of a publication of an edition.
uri.note: A publication requires `content_hash` (`LDC-E1305`). Its bytes are not part of the CLIR; without `local_path` they do not resolve locally and the §194 checks do not run.

jurisdiction.title: Source jurisdiction
jurisdiction.summary: The legal order a source belongs to, written as an institution identifier.
jurisdiction.note: An institution identifier (StableId), not a term: it needs no declaration, is not type-checked and is compared by equality. It is not the std type `Jurisdiction`.

timezone.title: Calendar time zone
timezone.summary: The time zone of a calendar snapshot.
timezone.note: A calendar without `timezone_db` or with an incomplete `period` is an error before evaluation: holidays and working days are snapshot data, not operating-system settings.

quantity.title: Duration parameter
quantity.summary: An expansion parameter holding the duration of a term, used in the date term of a deontic window.
quantity.note: The argument is a quantity literal of a term unit (`10 calendar_day`) or a `Quantity` binder. It is not declared in `for` and does not become a rule variable.

integer.title: Integer parameter
integer.summary: An expansion parameter holding a whole number: the threshold of an aggregate premise.
integer.note: The argument is an integer literal or the name of an `Integer` binder parameter.

option.title: Optional premise parameter
option.summary: An expansion parameter for a premise that may be absent.
option.note: The instance must choose explicitly: `some r` or `none`. Omitting the field is an error.

list.expansion.title: List parameter
list.expansion.summary: An expansion parameter holding a finite list of relation references.
list.expansion.note: `min N` is the least length; `min 0` allows an empty list. The instance passes `[r1, r2, …]`.

list.aggregate.title: List aggregate
list.aggregate.summary: Collects the outputs of all matching rows of a decision table into a list.
list.aggregate.note: A final `otherwise` is forbidden here: no match gives `[]`. The return type must be `List<T>`; matching rows are ordered by canonical row ID.

decision.title: Named pure decision
decision.summary: Names a pure query over evaluated legal state: one table or let* plus return, no norms or effects.
decision.note: A nested rule is not a decision body: the compiler answers a migration diagnostic. A decision creates no norm or effect.

source.title: Source work
source.summary: Declares the abstract Work behind an act: its kind, jurisdiction, authority and number.
source.note: A source is the abstract Work, not its text: content and language live in edition, the file in publication.

case.title: Case file
case.summary: Pins one matter to decide: its evaluation context, named individuals and asserted facts with evidence.
case.note: A case is computation input, not a norm: it creates no program node. Assertion arguments must be ground terms, never computed calls.

priority.title: Rule priority
priority.summary: Orders conflicting rules: prefer the winning application over the losing one, with an explicit reason.
priority.note: Priority resolves only opposite conclusions: two heads of one polarity never conflict, however different. A cycle gives PRIORITY_CONFLICT, never a silent tie-break.

evidence.title: Evidence document
evidence.summary: Declares a case document: a stable id over a typed schema with provenance fields.
evidence.note: Evidence is case input, not program: in a package it warns (E1314) and is refused without status (E1208). The core never derives admissibility from a count.

context.title: Named context profile
context.summary: Pins reusable evaluation axes under one versioned name: jurisdiction, time, resolvers and policies.
context.note: A profile sets no hidden defaults: the case extends it by name and states its own legal time. Extra fields must be namespaced.

constraint.title: Non-derivational check
constraint.summary: States a mandatory relation between decided facts: when the antecedent holds, the requirement must hold too.
constraint.note: A constraint derives nothing: no support, no defeat, no sanction. Its failure is a validation finding; a legal consequence needs a separate rule.

interpretation.title: Named reading
interpretation.summary: Groups rules, priorities and definitions as one reading of a named document, with status and authority.
interpretation.note: of names the interpreted document: include carries the whole canonical expansion, and a cross-package include is rejected.

stage.title: Reserved tour boundary
stage.summary: Reserves a named node for round-based stratification: an empty body stays a loud boundary.
stage.note: A reserved stage never executes: evaluation stops with NON_EXECUTABLE_STAGE. Indexed bodies need law.core 0.2.4 or later.

Unit.title: Unit tag surface
Unit.summary: The declared name for measurement-unit tags: tags resolve in the unit registry, conversions stay explicit.
Unit.note: Unit is not an annotatable type: it stays out of the compiler type dictionary (E-0039), so never write x: Unit.

support.title: Support edge
support.summary: Links one document to one proposition with a fixed relation: supports, refutes, authenticates, measures, reports or establishes.
support.note: Support lives in the case with evidence: a package-level edge warns (E1314). Name the policy that backs the link.

unit.title: Unit declaration
unit.summary: Declares a measurement unit: a simple atom carries exact scale and dimension, a derived unit multiplies simple ones.
unit.note: Scale is an exact positive rational pair, never rounded: unknown tags, cycles and zero scale are static errors.

calendar.title: Calendar dataset
calendar.summary: Declares a versioned calendar dataset binding: timezone, period and a content-addressed resource.
calendar.note: content_hash pins the dataset bytes, not the CLIR node: the compiler hashes the node separately. The executor never reads bytes at resource directly.

snapshot.title: Snapshot function
snapshot.summary: Declares an external function deterministic only against an exact snapshot hash, under a named capability.
snapshot.note: Determinism is relative to the snapshot, never absolute: a scenario snapshot must carry programHash, checked against the requesting program.

fragment.title: Source fragment
fragment.summary: Pins one addressable passage inside an edition: kind, locator and fixed text.
fragment.note: A fragment needs a stable id: the article number is locator metadata, never identity by itself.

Event.title: Domain event
Event.summary: Declares an immutable nominal event subtype with typed intrinsic fields; identity is the stable id.
Event.note: For executable temporal use carry exactly one canonical time: Interval<Instant>, or an explicit mapping policy to one.

language.title: Language header
language.summary: Opens every file: the language name and the exact version the file is written against.
language.note: The version is checked exactly against the registry: 0.1.0 is not 0.1, and an unknown version is E1401.

edition.title: Source edition
edition.summary: Pins one content-language-revision Expression of a source: language, officiality and lifecycle.
edition.note: An edition is content, not a file: one edition may carry several publications without changing any norm.

assert.title: Assertion
assert.summary: Asserts one proposition as fact, with id, origin, validity window and evidence links.
assert.note: Arguments must be ground terms: computed calls never match silently (E1325). A duplicate anonymous assert is refused (E1331).

closure.title: Closed-world scope
closure.summary: Bounds explicit negation: only inside predicate, domain and snapshot may absence become false.
closure.note: The scope must be finite and precise: without a valid closure, absence of a record proves nothing.

const.title: Named constant
const.summary: Binds an immutable snapshot value to a name: numbers, money, or an individual via entity_ref.
const.note: An individual gets a name only through const plus entity_ref: the call alone is a value, not a name. Mutable facts are relations.

map.title: Total enum map
map.summary: Declares a closed total mapping from one enum to another: sugar over a pure function.
map.note: Totality is proven, not promised: a missed or repeated member is a static error (E1326). Both enums live in this package.

reference.title: Dynamic reference
reference.summary: Declares a reference resolved at evaluation: source, locator, resolution axis and policy.
reference.note: resolve_at is mandatory (E1307): in 0.1 the only axis is legal_time. The resolved static reference lands in the input manifest.

state.title: Automaton state
state.summary: Names one state of a procedure automaton: entry states are initial, sinks are terminal.
state.note: State names are unique across the whole package (E1351): a case addresses a member by its bare name, so two procedures cannot share one.

test.title: Executable test
test.summary: Pins one executable check: given holds the case, evaluate asks the question, expect states the verdict.
test.note: A test is input and expectation, not a norm: it creates no program node. The given case needs no context block to compile.

procedure.title: Procedure automaton
procedure.summary: Declares a state automaton over one instance: named states plus the transitions between them.
procedure.note: Exactly one state is initial (E1311): the automaton has a single entry. The instance parameter is mandatory: guards read it.

action.title: Action with actor
action.summary: Declares an event with a designated actor: an action someone performs, with typed fields.
action.note: Declaring an action creates no permission or duty by itself. Like events, actions are immutable nominals with a stable id.

publication.title: Published file
publication.summary: Pins one published file of an edition: media type, retrieval address and content hash.
publication.note: content_hash is mandatory (E1305): identity is the bytes. Without local_path the text-inclusion checks do not run (E5206).

definition.title: Exact definition
definition.summary: Defines a concept by exact condition: the head holds exactly when the body holds.
definition.note: Use exact for both directions, necessary for a constraint; a one-way derivation is a strict rule.

record.title: Value record
record.summary: Bundles typed fields under one name: the plain value object of the language.
record.note: Records bundle named values, nothing more: decision tables read them by field, as input.income. A record derives nothing.

use.title: Explicit selection
use.summary: Selects records explicitly: in a case, use names a snapshot alias and the records taken from it.
use.note: Between files, use self::{...} needs [authoring] local_imports=explicit in the manifest, otherwise E1118. Name every record taken.

derived.title: Derived unit
derived.summary: Declares a derived unit as a product and quotient of simple ones: it has no scale of its own.
derived.note: Unlike a simple atom, a derived unit carries no own scale: it computes from its factors. Unknown factors and cycles are static errors.

term.title: Legal term with cases
term.summary: Writes one legal deadline with a general rule and named special cases.
term.note: from takes the single Date binder exactly once, due drops the date, default is mandatory: the lowering builds rules plus a priority. No policy lives inside term.

enum.title: Enumeration
enum.summary: Declares a closed set of named members: the total vocabulary of one choice.
enum.note: Closed means closed: maps over an enum prove totality (E1326 on a miss). Members are bare names, compared by identity.

transition.title: Automaton transition
transition.summary: Moves one procedure automaton from one state to another on an event, under a guard.
transition.note: from and to name states of the same procedure; the guard reads the instance parameter. Member names stay unique package-wide (E1351).

revision.title: Revision link
revision.summary: Links editions into an immutable graph: what came before, what comes next, and why.
revision.note: The graph is immutable: a consolidation is a new edition with provenance, never an edit. Name the relation: supersedes, amends, repeals.

deadline.title: Deadline policy
deadline.summary: Pins how calendar deadlines count: start day, end inclusion, rolling and cutoff.
deadline.note: The first three fields are mandatory; there is no ambient policy: without one the result is MISSING_POLICY, not a guess.

fiction.title: Legal fiction
fiction.summary: Deems an institutional fact true when its conditions hold: the law treats it as decided.
fiction.note: Strength after the name is mandatory: Core never picks one for you. A fiction concludes institutional facts, never empirical ones.

presumption.title: Presumption
presumption.summary: Holds a conclusion defeasibly until an exception fires: a rule, a defeater and a priority in one form.
presumption.note: scope, effective, source_anchor and metadata have no lowering here: in 0.1 they are refused (E0201), not silently dropped.

role.title: Legal role
role.summary: Introduces one LegalRole constant for an actor type, read through the has_role relation.
role.note: A role creates no membership and no relation: has_role stays the single standard relation. Only the const is new.

temporal_resolution_policy.title: Day-resolution policy
temporal_resolution_policy.summary: Pins how a Date becomes an Instant interval: one fixed offset and a day boundary.
temporal_resolution_policy.note: The offset is fixed and trusted, the IANA name is a label only: no tz database is ever read. DST-crossing windows need a pinned tz dataset instead.

classification.title: Classification
classification.summary: Supports a class by rule-like conditions: strict or defeasible strength.
classification.note: defeater is not a classification strength: a class is supported or separately excepted, never defeated in place.

expand.title: Expansion instance
expand.summary: Instantiates a named expansion: binds its parameters to local relations and values.
expand.note: Name the expansion first, then the instance, and label it (E1339 without one). Bind every parameter the expansion declares.

exports.title: Export map
exports.summary: Names what an expansion publishes: local names for generated nodes.
exports.note: exports maps a local name to a generated node (self/...): the instance binds params, the outside world reads exports.

counterfactual.title: What-if analysis
counterfactual.summary: Asks what minimal case change would flip a target: mutable and immutable inputs plus cost.
counterfactual.note: Exactly one cost is required (E1205): without it minimality is undefined. Immutable wins over mutable on every clash.

factors.title: Factor dictionary
factors.summary: Declares the closed factor vocabulary of one precedent line: signature, domain, sides and courts.
factors.note: The dictionary is closed: an undeclared factor does not exist for the profile. The domain binds every signature variable (E2701).

property.title: Property check
property.summary: States what must hold over generated inputs: a forall domain plus a pure expectation.
property.note: The domain must be finite and seeded, with the seed in the test manifest. A property observes the program, it never extends it.

precedent.title: Precedent case
precedent.summary: Records one decided case as factor sets and an outcome under a named vocabulary.
precedent.note: decided is mandatory: without a date the holding has no window. Overruling is declared by the overruled precedent itself, in its own package.

region.title: Parallel region
region.summary: Declares one token-holding area of a parallel state: its own states and transitions.
region.note: Each area owns exactly one token: a transition inside an area moves only that token. Every area needs its own initial state, and join stays explicit.

params.title: Expansion params
params.summary: Declares what an expansion instance must bind: binders, relations and value slots.
params.note: The instance binds each declared parameter by name: bind for binders, plain assignment for relations and values.

entrenchment.title: Entrenchment
entrenchment.summary: Shields one source passage over a time window: a locator plus its validity interval.
entrenchment.note: The locator shields itself and its /-children only: article/2 covers /paragraph/7, never /20. A touching revision op is refused (E5301).

align.title: Fragment alignment
align.summary: States that two fragments in different languages correspond, with review status.
align.note: Alignment creates no logical equivalence of formalizations: it is a review claim about texts, not a merged meaning.

interpretation_group.title: Reading alternatives
interpretation_group.summary: Groups rival readings of one document with a selection policy: exactly one, any, or composed.
interpretation_group.note: With exactly_one and no chosen alternative, dependent queries answer INTERPRETATION_REQUIRED: a result status, not a document failure.

verification.title: Verification record
verification.summary: Pins one external authenticity check of a case document: evidence, hash, verifier and outcome.
verification.note: The core never verifies: it accepts only when document_hash matches the bytes. Verification lives in the case, like the evidence it checks.

and.title: Conjunction
and.summary: Conjoins formulas: every conjunct must hold for the whole to hold.
and.note: Write every conjunct positively: not (A and B) is a static error, so name a predicate for the negative case instead.

scope.title: Rule scope
scope.summary: Restricts when a rule applies: a formula kept separate for indexing and explanations.
scope.note: Scope merges with when semantically: moving a condition changes nothing about cycles or barriers. At most one scope per block (E1329).

effective.title: Effective window
effective.summary: Bounds the rule to a legal-time interval: outside it the rule does not apply.
effective.note: effective is checked against context.legal_time. At most one per block (E1329); a constraint outside legal_time is skipped.

unless.title: Rule exception
unless.summary: Adds a defeasible exception to a rule: when it fires, the rule does not.
unless.note: `unless C` creates a defeater; `unless C then not A` creates a defeasible contrary rule with direct priority over the general rule. It is invalid on a strict rule.

collect.title: Comprehension
collect.summary: Builds a set or list by filtering: collect bindings of a type where a formula holds.
collect.note: collect x: T is a Set, collect all x: T is a List: the keyword all switches shape. Aggregates fold the result.

defeat.title: Defeater head
defeat.summary: Heads a defeater rule: removes support for the named conclusion without asserting anything.
defeat.note: A defeater never wins by strength: it blocks an equal or incomparable candidate, but a stronger rule beats it.

where.title: Filter clause
where.summary: Filters a comprehension or aggregate: only bindings satisfying the formula are collected.
where.note: where absorbs the whole formula, including and: the bindings it filters come from the collect line.

if.title: Conditional term
if.summary: Chooses between two data terms on a boolean: if the condition holds, the first, else the second.
if.note: Branches are data terms, not rule bodies. In rule heads, status tests are nonmonotone reads and may be refused by §111 (E-0176).

some.title: Present option
some.summary: Passes a present optional argument at an instance: some names the value the option carries.
some.note: some(...) as a data constructor is reserved (0.2): in 0.1 some lives only in expansion arguments and if some premises. none drops the premise.

as.title: Premise alias
as.summary: Names the unwrapped value of an if some premise: the binder the when-line reads.
as.note: import ... as ... is reserved in 0.1 (E0206): the package is addressed by name. In 0.1 as lives only in expansion premises.

governs.title: Temporal scope
governs.summary: Scopes a rule to regulated-fact time on a named axis: support outside the window is not support.
governs.note: The axis is judged by the support valid interval intersecting the window: a support without that axis never passes. Asserts carry no axis slot.

within.title: Aggregate window
within.summary: Bounds an event day to the instance window inside a count premise: day within window.
within.note: At most one aggregate premise per rule (E1335). The window binds by name and must be linked by a positive premise of the same rule.

set.title: Set literal (reserved)
set.summary: Reserved word of the set literal; a set is built by a `collect` comprehension.
set.note: The literal `set { … }` is declared by the grammar but reserved: no implementation parses it (`LDC-E0201`). Build a `Set<T>` with `collect x: T where F`, or list fixed values as an `enum`.

effect_terminate.title: Terminate effect
effect_terminate.summary: Names a terminate LegalEffect on a power (§127).
effect_terminate.note: This spelling identifies a LegalEffect kind. E0310 execution limits remain; no new effect executor is introduced.

effect_modify.title: Modify effect
effect_modify.summary: Names a modify LegalEffect on a power (§127).
effect_modify.note: This spelling identifies a LegalEffect kind. E0310 execution limits remain; no new effect executor is introduced.

protected_effect_terminate.title: Protected terminate effect
protected_effect_terminate.summary: Names the terminate effect protected by an immunity (§128).
protected_effect_terminate.note: This spelling identifies a LegalEffect kind. E0310 execution limits remain; no new effect executor is introduced.

poly_root_2.title: Quadratic root
poly_root_2.summary: Selects the k-th distinct real root of a degree-2 polynomial over the rationals.
poly_root_2.note: Rational roots are Number, irrational roots Algebraic. A whole Number index narrows exactly to Integer; a fractional index is TYPE_ERROR. An index outside the roots is DOMAIN_ERROR. Available from profile 0.6.

poly_root_3.title: Cubic root
poly_root_3.summary: Selects the k-th distinct real root of a degree-3 polynomial over the rationals.
poly_root_3.note: Rational roots are Number, irrational roots Algebraic. A whole Number index narrows exactly to Integer; a fractional index is TYPE_ERROR. An index outside the roots is DOMAIN_ERROR. Available from profile 0.6.
